decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a specialized, high-value system that is only a few years past its Q1/2019 release, and the firm's established dosimetry business gives it the slack to carry it while the particle therapy market builds up.

Small volume chambers are core consumables for small-field dosimetry in a stable, regulated market, and there is no evidence of a shortfall against aspirations that would prompt search for other uses of the resources.
It overlaps with Product B and so is the likelier candidate for portfolio pruning, but chamber families are routinely broad and it costs little to keep a model customers have validated.
The standard clinical chamber line with several models anchors absolute dosimetry and calibration services, so it likely meets aspirations and supports the core business.
The relative dosimetry chamber pairs with the firm's water phantoms and its connected QA workflow, so it reinforces the established business rather than draining resources.
Thimble chambers are long-lived standard products with steady clinical demand, and nothing indicates a shortfall that would justify dropping this one.
